svg.title: Caddy, Janus, and Rip Server architecture
svg.desc: Caddy terminates public traffic and sends admitted requests to Janus. Janus provides a hot registry, control API, request pipeline, ten edge capabilities, Unix worker routing, and a reload-safe hub. Rip Server registers, heartbeats, publishes workers, and uses a doorbell to reload on demand.
svg.text: Cold edge policy, hot tenant registration, and disposable workers — in one implementation-backed map
Caddy is the edge; Janus is compiled into it as an app, HTTP handler, and logging encoder.
Final upstream X-Sendfile is transformed by Janus; worker busy/draining signals may retry safely.
internal Unix · local HTTP · public HTTPS
hub publish · access stream · live stats
Hot JSON changes registry state, never cold admission.
Registry + generations · least-conn data plane · hubs
mDNS advertiser · auth sessions · browse leases · access bridge
Reload keeps registrations and WebSockets; process restart clears registry.
The tenant announces itself; Janus does not supervise it.
POST app: name + host/site + files + upstreams
Heartbeat every 5s · DELETE on clean stop
bridge_path is optional hot state; the manager does not emit it.
Ordered roots · cache policy · proxy-first prefixes
optional SPA shell · browse flag · patterned {site}
The original request body stays unread until fresh sockets are visible in Janus.

g.text: Janus re-resolves and streams the original request once
Hub WebSockets never leave the edge

svg.text: Ten shipped capabilities, plus the registry-driven host router, heartbeat reaping, TLS allowlisting, and least-connection Unix proxy.

g.text: LAN names + redacted status front door

svg.text: Memory-only registry · tenants re-register after process restart
